title.value: B UGS IN THE D ATA : H OW I MAGE N ET M ISREPRESENTS B IODIVERSITY
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote: B UGS IN THE D ATA : H OW I MAGE N ET M ISREPRESENTS B IODIVERSITY

extractions.description: The paper analyzes the 13,450 images from 269 classes that represent wild animals in the ImageNet-1k validation set, with the participation of expert ecologists. It finds that many of the classes are ill-defined or overlapping, and that 12% of the images are incorrectly labeled, with some classes having >90% of images incorrect. It also finds that both the wildlife-related labels and images included in ImageNet-1k present significant geographical and cultural biases, as well as ambiguities such as artificial animals, multiple species in the same image, or the presence of humans.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper directly addresses issues related to biodiversity and the accurate representation of wildlife in a widely used dataset, which is crucial for building reliable machine learning models for ecological applications.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Our findings highlight serious issues with the extensive use of this dataset for evaluating ML systems, the use of such algorithms in wildlife-related tasks, and more broadly the ways in which ML datasets are commonly created and curated.

primary_category.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on the misrepresentation of biodiversity in the ImageNet-1k dataset, which directly relates to the protection and understanding of natural systems.
primary_category.quote: Here, we examine the 269 classes of wild animals in ImageNet-1k, working with expert ecologists to evaluate both the class definitions and the images included in each class.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper specifically investigates the accuracy and biases in the representation of wild animal species within the ImageNet-1k dataset, making biodiversity the most relevant sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: Our findings also raise significant concerns about various real-world ML applications where ImageNet-1k is used, as well as highlighting the fundamental importance of domain expertise in crafting ML benchmark datasets.

applications.justification: The paper discusses the use of ImageNet-1k for evaluating ML models used in wildlife-related tasks, which includes species identification and monitoring.
applications.quote: Our findings highlight serious issues with the extensive use of this dataset for evaluating ML systems, the use of such algorithms in wildlife-related tasks, and more broadly the ways in which ML datasets are commonly created and curated.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not suggest a new primary category.
